The UGREEN 100W is the strongest verified option here if you want to charge a laptop without carrying another cable. The UGREEN 65W is the notable trap: its retractable cable stops at 60W. Actual draw can be lower depending on the device, charging protocol, and whether other ports are occupied.

I limited the table to models for which I could establish the cable's output, rather than assuming it matches the charger's advertised total. This is not an exhaustive market list, and I haven't independently tested the ratings.

chats.answer:
The important distinction is the maximum output through the built-in cable, not the wattage printed on the charger. Here are wall chargers I found with a retractable USB-C cable; the figures are for charging one device at a time.

Wall charger

	

Built-in cable output

	

Cable length




Anker Nano 35W Retractable Charger

—

65W

UGREEN Nexode 65W Retractable

	

60W

UGREEN Nexode 100W Retractable

	

100W

	

2.5 ft

Anker lists its Nano as a 35W charger with the cable built in, and PhoneSuit explicitly rates its retractable cable at 65W. 
Anker US
 The UGREEN 65W model is the notable trap: its separate USB-C port can supply 65W, but the retractable cable is limited to 60W. UGREEN explicitly confirms the full 100W through the cable on its 100W model. 
UGREEN US
+2

Other options include the Belkin Retractable 45W, Belkin Retractable 67W, and UGREEN Nexode 45W Retractable. I found those models, but the specifications I retrieved did not unambiguously separate cable output from charger output, so I would not treat their headline wattages as verified cable ratings.

For a laptop, I'd choose the UGREEN 100W if you want the most verified power without carrying another cable, or the PhoneSuit for a verified 65W option. I focused on plug-in wall chargers, excluding power banks and car chargers; this is a verified shortlist, not an exhaustive market survey. Actual charging power can be lower depending on your device and whether other ports are in use.
